ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are two blue straight lines slanting downward to the right, and they have the same pink arrow markings, indicating that these two lines are parallel. On the left side, there is also a blue straight line slanting upward to the right, intersecting these two parallel lines respectively. ∠1 is located at the upper-left intersection, ∠5 and ∠6 are located at the lower-left intersection, and ∠5 and ∠6 are adjacent and form a straight line. Reasoning: Because the two straight lines slanting downward to the right are parallel, and the straight line on the left slanting upward to the right is a transversal, ∠1 is equal to ∠6 in the corresponding position at the lower intersection. Therefore m∠6 = m∠1 = 53°. Also because ∠5 and ∠6 are a linear pair and their sum is 180°, m∠5 = 180° - 53° = 127°.

raw_record.question_text: In the figure, $m\angle 1 = 53$. Find the measure of $\angle 5$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the two downward-sloping blue lines are marked parallel, and the left upward-sloping blue line intersects both of them. Angle 1 is at the upper intersection on this left transversal, while angle 5 is at the lower intersection. Use the corresponding-angle relationship to transfer the given angle: the angle at the lower intersection in the same relative position as angle 1 is angle 6, so m∠6 = 53°. Then read from the image that ∠5 and ∠6 are adjacent angles forming a straight line at the lower-left intersection, so they are a linear pair. Therefore m∠5 = 180° - 53° = 127°.
